boilerplate.general_comments_title: General Comments about the Quantitative Reasoning Section
general_comments: The figures accompanying some of the problems are provided to help solve the problems, but are not necessarily drawn to scale.  Therefore, do not rely on the figures alone to deduce line length, angle size, and so forth.
If a line in a figure appears to be straight, you may assume that it is in fact a straight line.
When a geometric term (side, radius, area, volume, etc.) appears in a problem, it refers to a term whose value is greater than 0, unless stated otherwise.
When \(\sqrt{a}\) (a > 0) appears in a problem, it refers to the positive root of a.
"0" is neither a positive nor a negative number.

clusters.intro: Study the table below, then answer the four questions that follow. Nine players, A through I, held a tournament of board games, consisting of games of four types. Two players took part in each game in the tournament, and every game ended in a win for one of them. The games were arranged according to the order of the players: first player A played against all the players in order, then player B played against all the players except A, whom he had already played against, and so on, until each player had played once against every other player. Each game in the tournament is represented in the table by a cell. The row and the column indicate the players taking part in the game, the shape indicates the type of game, and the arrow indicates the winner – "→" indicates that the player appearing at the beginning of the row won; "↑" indicates that the player appearing at the head of the column won. Finally, the number in the cell is the number of points with which the winner won the game (see key). For example: Player B played against player E at "Dangerous Spin". Player E won, and won with 4 points.

Study the graph below, then answer the five questions that follow. The graph presents data on the grades of 50 students who were tested in two exams – one at the beginning of the year and one in the middle of the year. The vertical axis shows the grades received in the exams (from 1 to 10). One of the grades is written in each black rectangle (according to the position of the rectangle in relation to the vertical axis). The black rectangle and the arrows going out from it represent all the students who received at the beginning of the year the grade written in the rectangle. An upward arrow (grey) represents the students whose grade in the middle of the year was higher than at the beginning of the year. A number is written in a circle inside the arrow, and the tip of the arrow represents the highest grade received among these students. A downward arrow (white) represents the students whose grade in the middle of the year was lower than at the beginning of the year. A number is written in a circle inside the arrow, and the tip of the arrow represents the lowest grade received among these students. Note: No student received the same grade in both exams. For example, out of the students who received the grade 7 at the beginning of the year, there are 3 students who received a higher grade in the middle of the year. The highest grade received among these students is 9.

In the accompanying figure the point O is the origin.
OABC is a rectangle two of whose sides are tangent to the circle at the points D and E.

Based on this information and the information in the figure,
CE = ?

methods.text: \(|x-y|\) and \(|y-x|\) are the same distance measured in opposite directions, and distance has no direction. The two terms are identical, so the difference is 0.
\(x=5,\ y=2\): \(|3|-|-3|=3-3=0\). Any pair gives the same thing, which is the clue that this is an identity rather than a calculation.

questions.stem:
The price of a dress on the second day rose by 100% compared with the price on the first day, on the third day it rose by 50% compared with the price on the second day, and on the fourth day it rose by 25% compared with the price on the third day.

By what percentage did the price of the dress rise on the fourth day compared with the first day?

methods.text: The factors multiply: \(2 \times 1.5 \times 1.25 = 3.75\). A price of 3.75 times the original is a rise of 275%.
The rise is \(3.75 - 1 = 2.75\), which is 275% — not 375%. Converting a multiplier into a percentage increase means subtracting 1 first.

3 pumps operating at the same fixed rate pump 5 litres of water per hour together.

In how many hours will 2 pumps pump 20 litres of water together?

methods.text: Three pumps make 5 litres an hour, so one makes \(\frac53\) and two make \(\frac{10}{3}\).
\(20 \div \frac{10}{3} = 6\) hours. Reduce to a single pump before scaling up.
\((a-1)\left(a^2+a+1\right)\) is the difference-of-cubes identity read backwards: it equals \(a^3-1\). So \(a^3-1 = b^3-1\), giving \(a^3 = b^3\) and, both being positive, \(a = b\).
Take \(a=2\): the left side is \(1 \times 7 = 7\), so \(b^3 = 8\) and \(b = 2\). The two are equal, which only option (1) allows.

Ruti had a snake and a lizard.  A year ago the length of the snake was exactly 2 times the length of the lizard.
In the course of the year each of them grew longer by the same number of cm.
Now the snake is longer than the lizard by 36 cm.

What was the sum of the lengths of the snake and of the lizard a year ago (in cm)?
options: It cannot be determined from the information given

methods.text: Both grew by the same amount, so the gap between them never changed — it was 36 cm a year ago too. With the snake then twice the lizard, the gap equalled the lizard's length, so the lizard was 36 and the snake 72. Sum: 108.
Writing it out: \((2L+g) - (L+g) = L = 36\). The growth \(g\) cancels, which is why option (4) is wrong — the answer does not depend on the unknown growth at all.

questions.stem: The letters A and B represent digits between 1 and 9. AB is a two-digit number smaller than twice the sum of its digits. \(\dfrac{B}{A}\) = ?

methods.text: \(\overline{AB} < 2(A+B)\) means \(10A + B < 2A + 2B\), so \(8A < B\). Since \(B\) is at most 9, the only possibility is \(A = 1\) and \(B = 9\).

Place value makes the tens digit ten times as heavy in the number as in the digit sum, so the inequality is extremely tight — it can only survive with the smallest possible tens digit and the largest possible units digit.

questions.stem:
Three of the four following expressions are equal in value.

Which is the remaining expression?

methods.text: Reduce each to a power of 2: \(\left(\frac14\right)^{-5}\cdot\frac12 = \frac{2^{10}}{2} = 2^9\); \(\left(\frac12\right)^{-3}\cdot2^6 = 2^9\); \(8^3 = 2^9\); \(4^6 = 2^{12}\). The odd one out is \(4^6\).
Three of four being equal is the instruction to convert everything to one base. Once they are all powers of 2 the comparison is a glance.

Given:  x is a prime number greater than 2.

The value of the expression  \(\dfrac{x^{(x+1)}}{2^x}\)  is necessarily –

methods.text: A prime above 2 is odd, so \(x\) is odd and \(x+1\) is even. The numerator \(x^{x+1}\) is a power of an odd number, so it is odd — and it contains no factor of 2 at all.

The denominator \(2^x\) is therefore never cancelled, so the quotient is not an integer. And since \(2^x\) grows far faster than needed — at \(x=3\) it is \(\frac{81}{8}\), which is above 1 — check the size: for \(x=3\) the value exceeds 1, so it is a non-integer greater than 1.

questions.stem:
In the accompanying figure is a circle whose centre is O.
The area of the grey sector is \(\pi\) cm².

What is the length of the radius of the circle (in cm)?
Given: x ≤ y y ≤ z z ≤ x Which of the following statements is necessarily true?

methods.text: The three conditions close into a loop: \(x\) to \(y\) to \(z\) and back to \(x\). The chain gives \(x\le z\), and the third condition gives \(z\le x\). Both can hold only if \(x=z\), and that collapses everything between them.
It looks like too little information and is actually too much. A student who does not spot the loop will hunt counterexamples for a full minute and find none, because there are none.

questions.stem: Hadas wrote in a row all the two-digit numbers. Beneath it, in a second row, she wrote the sum of the digits of each number (see the illustration in the figure). Which of the following numbers appeared the fewest times in the second row?

methods.text: For two-digit numbers the digit sum runs from 1 to 18. Sums in the middle have many ways to be made; sums at the extremes have few. So the rarest is whichever listed sum is furthest from the middle.
Count them: sum 17 comes only from 89 and 98 — two ways. Sum 15 has four, sum 6 has six, sum 4 has four. So 17 is the fewest.

A car race was held on a track on which there are 4 numbered marking points (see figure). The routes between every two adjacent marking points are equal in length. In the race they go around the track a number of times. Car A and car B set out at the same moment from marking point 1 and began to travel on the track in a clockwise direction (see figures). Car A travels at a speed of v kph, and car B travels at a speed of 2v kph. At which marking point did the two cars meet for the first time (after the beginning of the race)?

methods.text: Same direction on a closed track, so B gains on A at \(2v - v = v\). They meet when B has gained one full lap.
Gaining a lap means B has covered two laps while A covered one — and A is then back at the start. The first meeting is at marking point 1, whatever the track's shape or the number of marks.

questions.stem:
Given:  a and b are numbers different from 0.

\(\left(\dfrac{b}{a} + \dfrac{a}{b}\right)^2\) = ?

methods.text: Squaring a sum: \(\left(\frac ba + \frac ab\right)^2 = \frac{b^2}{a^2} + 2\cdot\frac ba\cdot\frac ab + \frac{a^2}{b^2}\), and the middle term is \(2\) because the two fractions are reciprocals.
Take \(a=1, b=2\): the expression is \(\left(2+\frac12\right)^2 = 6.25\). Option (3) gives \(4+2+0.25 = 6.25\); the others give 4, 4.25 and 8.25.

questions.stem:
The number of elementary schools in Nes Tziona is greater by 2 than the number of elementary schools in Yavne.
The number of elementary schools in Yavne is greater by 9 than the number of elementary schools in Kiryat Shmona.

Which of the following numbers can be the total number of elementary schools in the three cities?

methods.text: Let Yavne have \(Y\). Then Nes Tziona has \(Y+2\) and Kiryat Shmona has \(Y-9\). The total is \(3Y - 7\).
So the total is 7 less than a multiple of 3, that is \(\equiv 2 \pmod 3\). Checking digit sums: 41 gives 5, and \(41+7 = 48\) is divisible by 3 ✓. The others fail.

questions.stem: a and b are two integers, greater than 1, and different from each other. c is an integer greater than \(a \cdot b\), and it is divisible both by a and by b without a remainder. Nir claimed: “From this it necessarily follows that c is divisible by \(a \cdot b\) too without a remainder.” Which of the following triplets of numbers shows that Nir's claim is wrong?

methods.text: Nir's claim fails exactly when \(a\) and \(b\) share a factor, because then \(\text{LCM}(a,b)\) is smaller than \(ab\). So you are hunting an option where \(a\) and \(b\) are not coprime.

\(a=6,\ b=4\) share a factor of 2, and \(c=36\) is divisible by both while \(ab = 24\) does not divide 36. Also check \(c > ab\): \(36 > 24\) ✓. The other options have coprime pairs, where the claim holds.
